name: Multiplane parallax
summary: Flat layers move at different speeds by their distance, so that a flat picture gets depth.
how: Move each layer at a speed in proportion to its distance: a far layer at 20% to 50% of the speed of the front layer.
Use 3 to 5 layers; more layers add load and no depth.
Give a reduced-motion setting that stops the shift of the layers.

origin.note: Disney's multiplane camera moves painted glass layers at different speeds; The Old Mill (1937) is its first film.

adoptions.via: Moon Patrol scrolls 3 background layers at different speeds in arcades.
16-bit consoles scroll 2 to 4 hardware layers for parallax depth.
Parallax scroll pages move the background layers slower than the page.
Layered app icons on tvOS, and later visionOS, tilt their layers with parallax.

sources.title: Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston, The Illusion of Life: Disney Animation (1981)
